investigator.method: Level 1 PASSIVE_STATIC only: curl (plain HTTP GET, descriptive User-Agent, no authentication, no browser/JS execution) against the venue's own official homepage (a Rails/Turbolinks app whose homepage itself lists upcoming events as static server-rendered cards) and two individual event detail pages, each of which additionally embeds a schema.org MusicEvent JSON-LD block. Cross-checking the JSON-LD startDate against the same cards' own directly-stated local time fields across both sampled events revealed a real, consistently-reproduced timezone-offset bug in the JSON-LD field, documented honestly below rather than trusted at face value.

probe_history.reason: A plain curl GET of the venue's official homepage (https://astra-berlin.de/) immediately exposed upcoming events as fully server-rendered static HTML event cards, each carrying a machine-readable 'data-realdate' datetime+offset attribute plus separate Doors/Start time-value elements, a title, and an event kind. Two sampled event detail pages additionally each embedded a schema.org MusicEvent JSON-LD block (title/url/location all directly correct) and a fully structured two-tier price block (Abendkasse/Vorverkauf). No further escalation was needed; Level 1 fully answered the investigation question, including surfacing a genuine data-quality caveat in the JSON-LD's own startDate offset.

venue_reference: Astra Kulturhaus (mid-size concert venue on the RAW site, Revaler Str. 99, Friedrichshain, Berlin)

identity.notes: The retained homepage's own <title> reads 'Astra Berlin | Home'. Independently, both sampled event detail pages' own JSON-LD directly states location.name 'Astra Berlin' and location.address 'Revaler Str. 99, 10245 Berlin', matching the venue's known RAW-site address — a second, distinct retained artifact confirming identity. The site's own JSON-LD self-references the 'www.astra-berlin.de' hostname as a variant of the same domain; the bare 'astra-berlin.de' hostname used to fetch all evidence here also returned HTTP 200 directly.

site_classification.platform: Ruby on Rails (Turbolinks) custom site. The homepage itself server-renders upcoming events as static cards (data-realdate attribute + separate Doors/Start time-value elements). Each event's own detail page additionally embeds a schema.org MusicEvent JSON-LD block using single-quoted script attributes (<script type='application/ld+json'>) — title/url/location are directly correct, but startDate was found, across two independently sampled events, to always literally state the local wall-clock time suffixed with a fixed, incorrect '+00:00' offset rather than the venue's true Europe/Berlin offset (see field_assessment.time notes and collector_assessment.blockers). No WordPress, Fourvenues, or Sanity signal detected; no ICS link found.

title.notes: The event detail page's own JSON-LD 'name' field, matching the homepage card's own <h1 class="event__title">.

start_date.notes: The event detail page's own JSON-LD 'startDate' date portion ('2026-09-05'), independently corroborated by the homepage card's own 'data-realdate="2026-09-05 19:00:00 +0200"' date portion and its separate 'event__date--full' text ('05.09.26') — all three directly-stated fields agree on the calendar date (only the JSON-LD's time-of-day/offset component is unreliable, handled separately under 'time').

time.notes: The event detail page's own JSON-LD 'startDate' ('2026-09-05T20:00:00+00:00') is NOT used as this field's basis: cross-checking two independently sampled events (Buzzcocks and SKI AGGU) showed this JSON-LD field always literally states the local wall-clock 'Start' time with a fixed, incorrect '+00:00' offset appended, rather than the venue's true Europe/Berlin offset — i.e. it is internally inconsistent with the same page's own other directly-stated fields, and is flagged as a collector_assessment blocker rather than trusted. Instead, the homepage card's own machine-readable 'data-realdate' attribute directly states a full local datetime WITH the correct UTC offset for this date ('2026-09-05 19:00:00 +0200') — but for the card's Doors time, not the Start time. The same card's own nested Start time-value element directly states the true performance start clock time ('20:00') with no offset of its own. Combining these two retained, first-party fields mechanically (see derivation) yields a single full UTC instant for the true show start: 2026-09-05T18:00:00Z (20:00 CEST).

derivation.rule: Each event card's own data-realdate attribute states a full local datetime with an explicit, correctly-formed UTC offset for that calendar date (representing Doors time). The same card's own nested Start time-value element states the true performance start clock time, with no offset of its own. Substitute the Start clock time for the data-realdate's time-of-day component, keeping data-realdate's own date and UTC offset unchanged, to produce one full UTC instant for the true show start. This derivation deliberately never uses the event detail page's own JSON-LD startDate field as an input, because that field was independently confirmed (via two sampled events) to always carry a fixed, incorrect '+00:00' offset suffix rather than the venue's real offset.

end.notes: Neither the event card, the event detail page, nor its JSON-LD state an end time.

venue_location.notes: The event detail page's own JSON-LD 'location.name'/'location.address' state this directly and identically on both sampled events.

source_record_id.notes: The event's own detail-page URL path segment (date + slug, e.g. '/events/2026-09-05-buzzcocks') is the site's own canonical, directly-stated permalink for that specific occurrence, matching the JSON-LD's own 'url' field exactly — the same documented URL-slug stable-identifier strategy already used for moog-barcelona-01/LAV and for the other AEG-operated Berlin venues already investigated in this trial.

event_url.notes: The event detail page's own JSON-LD 'url' field, stated directly.

price.notes: The event detail page's own structured price block directly states two named tiers ('Vorverkauf'/advance-sale and 'Abendkasse'/door-price) with exact amounts — a complete price breakdown, not merely a 'starting from' indicator.

blockers.description: This source's own JSON-LD 'startDate' field carries a confirmed, reproducible timezone-offset bug: across both independently sampled events it literally states the local wall-clock start time with a fixed, incorrect '+00:00' UTC-offset suffix (e.g. '2026-09-05T20:00:00+00:00' for an actual 20:00 CEST / 18:00Z show), rather than the venue's true Europe/Berlin offset. A naive JSON_LD collector implementation that trusts this field's offset literally would silently record every event's start time 2 hours late (summer) or 1 hour late (winter). Any future collector for this source MUST derive the UTC start instant from the homepage card's own data-realdate + Start time-value fields (see field_assessment.time.derivation) instead of parsing JSON-LD startDate directly, or must strip and recompute the offset using the venue's known fixed Europe/Berlin timezone. This must be resolved before activation.

reasons: Identity PROVEN from two independently retained artifacts (homepage title, and the JSON-LD's own location.name/address).
acquisition_class JSON_LD_EVENT, a resolved supported class, reached at Level 1 with no escalation needed.
A CONFIRMED public data path retained: the homepage's upcoming-events listing plus two sampled event detail pages with JSON-LD.
title, start_date, and time all PROVEN — time via a documented DETERMINISTIC_CONTEXT derivation that deliberately bypasses this source's own confirmed-buggy JSON-LD offset field.
source_record_id and venue_location and price all PROVEN with basis DIRECT_SOURCE — this source exposes a genuinely complete price breakdown, unlike the AEG-operated sibling venues in this trial.

recommended_family JSON_LD, an existing documented collector family — no new family required, though a MAJOR blocker documents that the standard JSON-LD startDate parsing path must NOT be used naively for this specific source.

Not advanced to READY_FOR_ACTIVATION: (1) an unresolved MAJOR blocker exists (the JSON-LD offset bug, which any real collector implementation must specifically work around), and (2) no DETERMINISTIC_DERIVATION offline-proof evidence item exists yet for the DETERMINISTIC_CONTEXT time field (gate 9/v1.2 offline-proof requirement) — both are separate follow-up work, not performed as part of this investigation task.
